title: White Chocolate Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: White chocolate melted into the custard with much less sugar; shaved white chocolate folded in.
summary: Our classic custard with white chocolate melted in and much less sugar, finished with shaved white chocolate. Creamy, mellow and gently sweet.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Warm the dairy
steps.text: Heat the cream, milk and half the sugar in the saucepan until steaming.

steps.title: Whisk the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks with the remaining sugar until pale. White chocolate brings plenty of sweetness, so only 60 g sugar is needed.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Whisk two ladles of hot dairy into the yolks, then return to the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Return the pan to low heat and stir until the custard thickens and hits 77-80 °C. Keep it below a simmer.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate
steps.text: Put the chopped chocolate in a clean bowl and sieve the hot custard over it. Leave for 1 min, then stir until smooth with the salt and vanilla; residual heat melts white chocolate gently without scorching it.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cool over the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn until thick, fold in the shaved chocolate and freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Use white chocolate with cocoa butter high on the label; cheaper bars do not melt smoothly.
A common mistake is melting white chocolate over direct heat, which makes it seize. Let the hot custard do the work.
Fresh raspberries are a great match.
storage: Freeze in a covered container for up to 2 weeks.
